in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

First of all, could you please tell me how many children you're looking to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names and ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! I'm looking to claim Child Benefit for my child Alex, who is 16 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information about Alex.

Since Alex is 16 years old, I need to ask a few more questions to determine your eligibility.

Is Alex currently in approved education (such as A-levels, Scottish Highers, or certain vocational qualifications) or training (such as an unpaid, employer-provided traineeship)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, Alex actually left school recently, but they've just registered with the local careers service to figure out what to do next.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know. That's helpful information.

Just to clarify, is the careers service that Alex registered with a **government-sponsored careers service** (such as the National Careers Service in England, Careers Wales, Skills Development Scotland, or the Careers Service in Northern Ireland)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, it's the National Careers Service - they went down there a few weeks ago to get some help with their options.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that. That's useful to know.

I have a couple more questions to check your eligibility:

Do you live in the UK, and does Alex live with you?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - we're in Manchester. And yes, Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that.

Just one more question to complete my assessment:

Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for providing all that information. I now have enough details to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, **you are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's a summary of why:

- ✅ You live in the UK (Manchester)
- ✅ Alex lives with you, meaning you're responsible for them
- ✅ Although Alex is 16 and has left education, they have registered with a government-sponsored careers service (the National Careers Service)
- ✅ No one else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex

**Important to note:** Because Alex has left education and registered with the National Careers Service, Child Benefit can continue for **up to 20 weeks** from when they left education. During this time, Alex may decide to return to approved education or training, start work, or take another path.

If Alex's circumstances change (for example, if they start working 24 hours or more per week, begin an apprenticeship, or start receiving certain benefits like Universal Credit), you would need to inform HMRC as this could affect your Child Benefit entitlement.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?
